slot_note: Root-Cause Analysis slot re-rooted at architecture 5 after architecture 4 was spent at stage 4, round 1 (lineage). One architecture per world: the epidemiology, econometrics, marketing and environmental worlds are closed to this slot; architecture 5 moves to Psychology and Behavioural Science, an invented English leisure trust's membership base, a new dataset and a new shell.
niche: a leisure trust's membership cancellations after a savings programme, read through members' lapsed attendance and the lag between a member's last visit and their cancellation
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads every file correctly compares each change's cancellations since 2 February 2026 with the same weeks of 2025 among the members it reached, finds the legacy terms letters behind the February spike and nothing yet from the Rewards closure, and books the year to the terms change, because they never count the members on the 2023 tariffs who stopped coming after Rewards closed and still pay, whom last year's lapsed members show will mostly cancel within the year.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is each change's cancellations through members' lapsed attendance, the indirect path a conditional process model carries from a change to attendance to cancellation, timed by the lag between a member's last visit and their cancellation (DellaVigna and Malmendier 2006 put it at 2.31 months on average over all cancellers; members who drift away rather than quit take about three); swap the members for a shop's customers or a clinic's patients and nobody keeps paying for a service they have stopped using, so the deciding quantity disappears.
layer1: membership register with tariff codes renamed at the 2023 migration and statuses as at the extract
cancellation requests from three channels with members asking twice
access-control weekly export with a turnstile outage week at one centre
letters posted in five batches with returned post
a care-call log keyed by membership number with its leading zeros dropped
class bookings with no-shows and cancellations
two Direct Debit bureaux with different dating, units and references, and household mandates
two reception till systems with different line grains, voids and refunds
a duty managers' log of pool shutdowns
stakeholder_role: the trust's head of membership, who must tell the council's April contract review which of February's changes the 2026-27 plan reverses

spine.entity: one membership's gate entries in one week

world.geography: England (an invented borough's charitable leisure trust)
world.org_type: charitable leisure trust running a borough's leisure centres under contract

driver: A rise in exits is booked to the change whose letters visibly triggered a spike, because the exits so far sit with the units that received them, but a second change made the same week stopped other units using the service without yet ending their subscriptions; those lapsed units still pay and will leave over the coming months at the rate earlier lapsed units did, so the year's cost belongs to the change whose exits have barely begun.
driver_concrete: Wrenford Leisure Trust's February 2026 savings programme moved legacy members onto the current terms at an unchanged price and closed the Rewards scheme in the same week; the legacy terms letters produced the visible spike in cancellations, but about twelve hundred members on the 2023 tariffs stopped coming after Rewards closed and are still paying at the 16 March extract, and at the rate last year's lapsed members cancelled over the following ten months the Rewards closure costs several times the terms change over the twelve months from 2 February 2026.
stump: A competent analyst compares each change's cancellations since 2 February with the same weeks of 2025 among the members it reached, finds the legacy terms letters behind the February spike and nothing yet from the Rewards closure, and recommends reversing the terms change, because they never count the 2023-tariff members who have stopped coming since the closure but have not yet cancelled, whom last year's lapsed members show will mostly cancel within the year.

differentiation.task122: task122 v2 re-attributes outcomes a log credits to the wrong session back to the exposure that produced them; here nothing is re-attributed: the decisive quantity is cancellations not yet made by members who have stopped coming, counted from their last visits and timed by last year's lapsed members, a forward count no record holds.
differentiation.task274: task274 completes defendants inside a recorded programme stage through the stage's own month-by-month termination hazard to size one randomised offer's effect; here no record marks a member as pending (the pending state is a relation between the visits record and a still-active membership), and the call ranks two changes made in one week whose timing biases run opposite ways: one change's exits arrived at once and were partly brought forward from later in the year, the other's are still to come.
differentiation.task402: task402 pairs each trip with the same section's restoration minutes before; nothing here is paired: the call turns on members who stopped coming and still pay, carried through last year's yield, against a change whose exits were only brought forward.
differentiation.task400: task400 reads a staggered rollout against the units not yet switched; here every change is in place at once on its own members, and the call turns on the exits still to come and the exits a reminder pulled forward.
differentiation.task230: task230 corrects a category count for the late part of an output still to be processed; here nothing is reclassified: the unobserved part is cancellations by lapsed payers, read from a stock against the same date a year earlier, and the rival change's exits net out within the year.

notes: Strategy maturity_censoring, gap time: the cancellations each change causes in the twelve months from 2 February 2026 are mostly unobserved at the 16 March 2026 extract for the Rewards closure (its lapsed members cancel on a lag of about three months from their last visit) and mostly observed for the legacy terms letters (they prompted long-lapsed legacy members at once). Gate G decomposition_attribution: the year's cancellations assigned to the right change. Calibration: last year's inactive members' ten-month outcomes (a realised roster). Shape 18: five filed changes are the hypotheses, each with its own in-place date and reach. Furniture redrawn against the live window: forum customer_or_counterparty (the council is the trust's contracting client; committee_or_panel, trustees_or_governors and executive_team are held by task400, task402 and task403), forcing event period_close (the 2025-26 year end sets the 2026-27 plan; vote_or_meeting and season_or_peak are held), role operations_director (product_manager is held by task403). lineage.architecture: v1 (Epidemiology and Public Health: a community trust's frailty virtual ward in an integrated care system's Core20 neighbourhoods, its pilot-year prevented admissions against care home closures)
lineage.driver: An intervention in one group is credited with a fall in that group's rate against the others', but between the baseline and evaluation periods the group's pool lost a block of its highest-rate members when the places that held them closed, so the baseline rate overstates what the smaller pool would have had; standardised to the evaluation period's mix on that property, which no column of the outcome or population files carries and a capacity record shows, the intervention's effect is a fraction of the difference in differences.
lineage.fate: spent at stage 2 on 2026-11-03 before any data was cut: with care home and community emergency admission rates set to published levels (about 0.70 against 0.24 to 0.58 a resident-year, a same-age ratio near two, not five), the composition lever fell to about 113 admissions for the 440 residents the closures moved, against a draw-to-draw spread of 157 to 215 in the default and the golden; a fixed bar between them separated them in 22 to 27 per cent of draws, and 72 per cent only at 1,400 residents moved, a failure no honest care group closure produces in one system's Core20 neighbourhoods.

lineage.architecture: v2 (Economics and Econometrics: a Saskatchewan farmland operator's canola yield panel, a new hybrid blamed for a 2026 shortfall that July heat in late-seeded fields' flowering windows caused)

world.geography: Canada, west-central Saskatchewan (invented farms in the Dark Brown and Black soil zones)

lineage.driver: A candidate change is blamed for a loss because its units lost more in the season it arrived, but the loss came from a short dated shock that harms a unit only inside a sensitive phase whose timing a clock sets from the unit's own start date at the pace of local conditions; the candidate's units started late for a one-off reason, so their sensitive phases met the shock, and read at equal timing the candidate costs nothing, while every season-wide, unit-level or linear start-date control leaves most of the loss on the candidate.
lineage.fate: spent 2026-11-03 at stage 2: the golden method's defensible variants straddle the bar, and flexible controls on a variable the default path already builds land the golden (flowering-window variants +2.1, -2.5, -12.0, +3.4, -8.2 and +4.9 per cent against a 5 per cent bar; seeding-week bins +3.6, a cubic +4.4 and same-day matching +9.3 on seeding dates the default's own rung 4 rebuilds, only a linear term still -10.1 or -8.3)

lineage.architecture: v3 (Marketing and Consumer Research: an invented GB domestic energy supplier's six-month new-customer satisfaction fall booked to the new billing platform that the May 2025 quote journey's understated quotes caused)

world.geography: Great Britain (an invented domestic energy supplier)

lineage.driver: A fall in a share of satisfied members is booked to the service the members' own ratings blame, because those ratings fell furthest and every later member was served by that service, but what moved is the gap between the amount each member was told to expect when they joined and the amount their own later use then cost, which no column holds and only the joining record set against the member's own measured use reveals; members told accurately are as satisfied as before on the same service.
lineage.fate: spent 2026-11-03 at stage 4, round 2: judge SEND_BACK on an ask's unfiled re-attribution (the golden overrode a registration's own quote reference), after a round-1 fix pass; the main call held both rounds

lineage.architecture: v4 (Physical and Environmental Sciences: an invented water and sewerage company's River Allery winter ammonia failures below the Coldmere Water Recycling Centre, booked to the new aeration control and nitrification capacity that a dairy's evening acid whey discharges caused)

world.geography: England, the East Midlands (an invented water and sewerage company's catchment; invented river, works and dischargers)

lineage.driver: A run of failures downstream of a shared processing unit is booked to that unit's own capacity and to a control change it made the same week, because the failures began then and the unit's own records validate it, but every one of them falls on the first or second day after a short discharge in one small contributor's own high-frequency record, which starves the unit's process for a day whatever the other contributors send; by load the contributor barely registers and its periodic strength samples and compliance read normal, so only its high-frequency record set against the unit's daily record and the downstream days shows the share each remedy can reach.
lineage.fate: spent 2026-11-04 at stage 4, round 1: the judge's blind derivation reached the call and every ask figure; effluent spikes from midnight on every failure day aligned one to one with the discharger's evening pH dips in its own monitor file, and the prompt's chart sentence announced the trace
